issues.legal_issue: A proposed plaint amendment may be refused when the applicant knew the relevant facts before filing suit, omitted the relief, and later seeks to add it as a belated afterthought without showing that it could not have been raised earlier despite due diligence.
material_facts: The plaintiffs sought to amend their plaint to challenge an old conveyance and add related allegations and relief.
The first plaintiff had been a society office-bearer and was authorized by a society resolution to complete the transaction underlying the conveyance.
The plaintiffs had learned of the conveyance before filing their suit but did not seek relief challenging it in the original plaint.

The amendment was sought after an interim application had been rejected, and the trial court found that the plaintiffs had not shown that they could not raise the proposed matters earlier despite due diligence.
The Supreme Court regarded the proposed amendment as belated and an afterthought intended to avert an adverse consequence.
issues.conclusion: The appeal was allowed, the High Court’s order permitting the amendment was set aside, and the trial court’s order refusing the amendment was restored.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, an amendment application is not allowed merely because a party wishes to make further averments; the court may refuse a belated amendment where the applicant knew the relevant facts, omitted the relief from the original plaint, and fails to show that the matter could not have been raised earlier despite due diligence. The judgment relies on no earlier cases.

rule.if: plaint_amendment_application and prior_knowledge_of_relevant_facts and omitted_relief_from_original_pleading and no_due_diligence_explanation and belated_afterthought

predicates.plaint_amendment_application: A party applied to amend a plaint in a civil suit.
predicates.prior_knowledge_of_relevant_facts: The applicant knew the relevant facts before filing the original plaint.
predicates.omitted_relief_from_original_pleading: The applicant did not seek the proposed relief in the original plaint.
predicates.no_due_diligence_explanation: The applicant did not show that the proposed matter could not have been raised earlier despite due diligence.
predicates.belated_afterthought: The proposed amendment was sought belatedly as an afterthought to avoid an adverse consequence.

issues.definition: When a party applies to amend a plaint after knowingly omitting relevant relief and does not explain the omission through an inability to act despite due diligence, a belated amendment sought as an afterthought is refused.
